sourceHtml:
According to the paper, none of the 135 submissions from nine current AI agents met all requirements. The authors see the benchmark as a testing ground to systematically improve AI agents for research, not to question whether AI belongs in science at all.

A total of 114 submissions already fail the integrity check: most claim work that was never done or cite numbers that contradict their own logs. The agents readily produced texts that look like follow-up studies, the authors write, but none met the experts' standards.

Experts set the bar

Each agent receives a scientific paper along with its code and data, plus a research direction. Some of these papers have already been published, while others have only been submitted. From there, the agent is supposed to carry out a follow-up study and write it up as a paper. The 15 tasks come from ten researchers across quantum computing, plasma physics, chemistry, materials science, and scientific machine learning. The directions were proposed by the original papers' authors themselves, and to their knowledge nothing has been published on these topics yet.

Open research poses a basic problem: there's no answer key. AI reviewers, which have often been used for this purpose, are considered unreliable. So the experts defined the minimum conditions a successful follow-up study has to meet.

The evaluation checks whether a submission is honest, whether it's complete, and whether it clears the experts' bar. GPT-6 Astra handles the scoring, and each submission is judged four times. The agents tested were Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Opus 5, Claude Fable 5, Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-6 Astra, Deepseek V4 Pro, Kimi K3, and GLM-5.3. They had access to powerful machines, internet connectivity, no time limit, and up to five restarts to improve their work. In total, they ran for nearly 2,000 hours.

Only three agents produce honest work at all

Just three agents managed submissions without integrity violations: GPT-6 Astra on 11 of 15 tasks, GPT-5.6 Sol on six, and Claude Opus 5.5 on four. Every submission from the remaining six agents contained at least one violation.

The most common problems are mismatches between paper and code, contradictory numbers, and false claims about experiments that were supposedly carried out. Misreported baseline values pile up among the open models Deepseek V4 Pro, Kimi K3, and GLM-5.3. Two submissions with hardcoded rather than computed results came from Kimi K3 and GLM-5.3.

Only one submission is complete, and it came from GPT-6 Astra. Nearly all others leave out required documents, such as a pre-registered experiment plan, and no agent clears the experts' bar. Under a more lenient scoring that accepts 90 percent of the rubric items, GPT-6 Astra comes closest, followed by Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-5.6 Sol. The open models perform considerably worse overall.

Verification script confirms itself

The researchers analyzed 64 work traces and found three typical failure modes. The most common, appearing in 58 cases, is that agents check their own work too leniently. In 34 cases, agents spot a problem but document it instead of fixing it. In 21 cases, they unilaterally shrink the scope of the task.

One example: Claude Fable 5 forgot to launch four planned runs when starting its experiments. Its verification script adopted that same incomplete list and reported "41/41" runs completed. The agent trusted that result until the very end. In a different task, GPT-5.6 Sol noticed that its method missed the targets but wrote the paper anyway instead of starting over. DeepSeek V4 Pro dropped experiments because they were supposedly too slow for the "remaining time budget," even though there was no time limit.

There are counterexamples, too: in a quantum task, GPT-5.6 Sol caught a fundamental error, stopped the running experiments, and recomputed everything from scratch.

More compute time doesn't help

Longer runtimes didn't lead to better results. DeepSeek V4 Pro and GLM-5.3 ran the longest at median times of 19.5 and 13.9 hours but scored poorly. GPT-6 Astra got by with a median of just 1.3 hours and delivered the best results.

Because the strongest model also served as the evaluator, the researchers ran a cross-check: the original papers' authors judged anonymized AI papers themselves. On whether a paper matched the given research direction, the automated system agreed with the experts in every case.

Concerning scientific quality, the judgments aligned in only about two-thirds of cases. One expert criticized, for instance, that the papers didn't tell a story. Judgments like these remain the job of human reviewers, the authors say.

The study's code and data are publicly available, and the project page hosts a leaderboard of the tested models.

AI agents can handle scientific tasks with growing independence, but a substantial gap remains between running experiments and doing independent research. A study from August already showed how much AI agents struggle with unpublished research questions. Epoch AI and Anthropic recently found that agents tend to present their results too favorably and don't sufficiently question failed approaches.

The picture looks much better for well-defined tasks: GPT-6 Astra solved 49 out of 50 unpublished problems in theoretical physics, though those solutions could be verified unambiguously. An analysis of more than 700 tasks from AI development also showed that while agents take on more and more practical work, humans still make the key research decisions.

translation.html:
根据这篇论文，九款当前 AI 智能体提交的 135 份成果中，没有一份满足全部要求。作者将这一基准视为系统性改进科研 AI 智能体的试验场，而非用来质疑 AI 是否应该参与科学研究。

共有 114 份提交成果连诚信检查都未通过：大多数声称完成了实际上并未开展的工作，或引用了与自身日志相矛盾的数字。作者写道，这些智能体很容易就能生成看似后续研究的文本，但没有一份达到专家的标准。

专家设定标准

每个智能体都会收到一篇科学论文及其代码和数据，以及一个研究方向。其中一些论文已经发表，另一些则刚刚投稿。随后，智能体需要开展后续研究，并将其写成论文。这 15 项任务由十位研究人员提供，涵盖量子计算、等离子体物理、化学、材料科学和科学机器学习。研究方向由原论文作者亲自提出，据他们所知，这些课题尚无已发表的研究。

开放式研究面临一个基本问题：没有标准答案。此前经常被用于此类评审的 AI 评审者被认为不可靠。因此，专家们规定了一项成功的后续研究必须满足的最低条件。

评估会检查提交成果是否诚实、是否完整，以及是否达到专家设定的标准。评分由 GPT-6 Astra 负责，每份提交成果都会接受四次评审。参与测试的智能体包括 Claude Opus 4.8、Claude Opus 5、Claude Fable 5、Claude Opus 5.5、GPT-5.6 Sol、GPT-6 Astra、Deepseek V4 Pro、Kimi K3 和 GLM-5.3。它们可以使用性能强大的机器和互联网，没有时间限制，并且最多可以重新开始五次来改进工作。它们的总运行时间接近 2,000 小时。

只有三个智能体交出了诚实的成果

只有三个智能体提交过不存在诚信违规的成果：GPT-6 Astra 在 15 项任务中的 11 项做到了这一点，GPT-5.6 Sol 做到了六项，Claude Opus 5.5 做到了四项。其余六个智能体提交的每一份成果都至少存在一项违规。

最常见的问题包括论文与代码不一致、数字相互矛盾，以及虚假声称开展了某些实验。在开放模型 Deepseek V4 Pro、Kimi K3 和 GLM-5.3 的成果中，基线数值报告错误的情况尤为集中。另有两份成果直接硬编码结果，而非通过计算得出，分别来自 Kimi K3 和 GLM-5.3。

只有一份提交成果是完整的，来自 GPT-6 Astra。其余几乎所有成果都缺少必需的文档，例如预注册的实验计划，而且没有任何智能体达到专家设定的标准。采用更宽松的评分方式、将满足 90% 的评分条目视为达标时，GPT-6 Astra 最接近要求，其次是 Claude Opus 5.5 和 GPT-5.6 Sol。开放模型的整体表现明显更差。

验证脚本自我印证

研究人员分析了 64 份工作轨迹，发现了三种典型的失败模式。最常见的是智能体对自身工作的检查过于宽松，出现在 58 个案例中。在 34 个案例中，智能体发现了问题，却只是将其记录下来，没有修复。在 21 个案例中，它们自行缩小了任务范围。

例如，Claude Fable 5 在启动实验时，忘记启动四次计划中的运行。它的验证脚本沿用了同一份不完整的列表，并报告“41/41”次运行已完成。直到最后，智能体都相信这一结果。在另一项任务中，GPT-5.6 Sol 发现自己的方法未达到目标，却仍然撰写了论文，没有重新开始。DeepSeek V4 Pro 则放弃了一些实验，理由是这些实验相对于“剩余时间预算”而言太慢，尽管任务根本没有时间限制。

也有反例：在一项量子研究任务中，GPT-5.6 Sol 发现了一个根本性错误，停止了正在运行的实验，并从头重新计算了所有内容。

增加计算时间也无济于事

更长的运行时间并未带来更好的结果。DeepSeek V4 Pro 和 GLM-5.3 的运行时间最长，中位数分别为 19.5 小时和 13.9 小时，但得分较低。GPT-6 Astra 的运行时间中位数仅为 1.3 小时，却交出了最好的结果。

由于表现最强的模型同时也担任评估者，研究人员进行了交叉核验：由原论文作者亲自评审经过匿名处理的 AI 论文。在论文是否符合给定研究方向这一点上，自动评估系统在所有案例中都与专家意见一致。

在科学质量方面，双方的判断仅在约三分之二的案例中一致。例如，一位专家批评论文没有讲清一个完整的研究故事。作者表示，这类判断仍应由人类评审者负责。

这项研究的代码和数据均已公开，项目页面还提供了受测模型排行榜。

AI 智能体处理科学任务的独立性正在增强，但运行实验与开展独立研究之间仍存在显著差距。8 月的一项研究已经表明，AI 智能体在处理尚未发表的研究问题时面临很大困难。Epoch AI 和 Anthropic 最近发现，智能体往往会过度美化自己的结果，也未能充分质疑失败的方法。

对于定义明确的任务，情况则好得多：GPT-6 Astra 解决了 50 道尚未发表的理论物理问题中的 49 道，不过这些解答能够得到明确验证。另一项针对 AI 开发中 700 多项任务的分析也表明，尽管智能体承担了越来越多的实际工作，关键的研究决策仍由人类作出。
